1970 Strange Situation: Why Quiet Babies Hid Racing Hearts

Inside the Study — In 1970 at Johns Hopkins University, developmental psychologists Mary Ainsworth and Silvia Bell observed fifty-six one-year-old infants across eight three-minute separations and reunions. Two decades later, Gottfried Spangler and Klaus Grossmann wired ECG heart monitors and salivary cortisol tests to reveal that outwardly silent avoidant toddlers carried surging physiological stress.
